sentences.text:
The Criminal Petition has been filed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (for brevity 'the Cr.P.C.,')/Section 528 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for brevity 'the BNSS') seeking to quash the docket order dated 14.10.2025 passed in S.C.(POCSO).No.185 of 2022 on the file of the learned Judge, Special Court for Trail of Offences under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, Kadapa, in Cr.No.06 of 2021 on the file of the Badvel U/G Police Station,
registered for the alleged offence punishable under Sections 366(A), 354(D), 376 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (for brevity 'the IPC'), Sections 3 and 4 of the POCSO Act, 2012.
2. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Assistant Public Prosecutor.
Perused the record.

3. As seen from the record, the allegation against the petitioner/Accused No.2 is that he is a friend of the junior paternal uncle of the victim, who has given some money to Accused No.1, with whom the victim is alleged to have eloped.
The age of the victim at the time of the alleged offence was 14 years.

4. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the Criminal Petition is disposed of with a direction that the petitioner/Accused No.2 Dr. YLR, J Dated 03.02.2026 shall appear before the learned Magistrate within a period of one week from this date.
On such appearance, the Non-Bailable Warrant issued against petitioner/Accused No.2 shall stand cancelled.
It is made clear that the petitioner/Accused No.2 shall appear before the learned Trial Court on each and every adjournment without fail.
5. With the above observation, the Criminal Petition is disposed of
As a sequel, Miscellaneous petitions, if any pending, shall stand closed.
DR. Y. LAKSHMANA RAO, J Date: 03.02.2026 RSI Dr. YLR, J Dated 03.02.2026
